Review priority of each site, for a directed review round of sheepdog

Source: R/fp_review_priority.R
fp_review_priority.Rd

Gives every site (every site and species, for a multispecies model) a size for sheepdog::select_directed(): the variance of its occupancy state given the data, \(q(1 - q)\), where \(q\) is the posterior probability that the site is occupied (occupied of fp_sites()). The size is largest, 0.25, where the model is least sure whether the species is present, and 0 where the data settle it. sheepdog then draws units with probability proportional to size and reviews one occasion of each.

Usage

fp_review_priority(
  object,
  species_code = NULL,
  validation = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

object

An fp_occu or fp_occu_ms object.

species_code

The label of the species in the predictions of sheepdog (its species_code, such as "Nyctidromus albicollis_Common Pauraque"). For an fp_occu model, a single label, required: without it, sheepdog would draw occasions of every species. For an fp_occu_ms model, optional: a character vector named by the species of the model, for when the model used other names (such as the short species of fp_read_sheepdog()); by default the species names of the model are taken as the labels.

validation

Optional data frame of reviewed clips, such as fp_read_sheepdog()$validation, with the columns site, verdict (TRUE for a confirmed detection) and, for a multispecies model, species_code. Units with a confirmed detection are left out.

ndraws

Number of posterior draws to use (all by default).

seed

Optional seed for the choice of draws.

Value

A data frame with one row per unit, sorted by decreasing size: site, species_code and size, the columns that sheepdog::select_directed() expects in its units. Sites and labels are text.

Details

Which units. The units are the sites, or the sites and species, the level of the occupancy state; sheepdog draws one occasion among the candidate occasions of each drawn unit. Units where the species is already known to be present are left out: those with a verified detection in the data of the fit, and those with a confirmed clip in validation (which may hold rounds reviewed after the fit). Without that, the floor of sheepdog (floor) would still draw them.

Why the variance. The size ranks units by how uncertain their state is, not by the exact gain of one review, which would also depend on the detection and false-positive rates of the occasion drawn. It is a simple rule, and it needs nothing beyond fp_sites().

Fitting a model to the directed rounds. The sizes depend only on data already in the fit, and sheepdog adds a floor, draws units at random given the sizes, and draws the occasion among those of the unit with a prediction at or above its threshold, detections the fit also holds when it uses the same threshold. A model fit to the data of all rounds (the earlier ones and the directed one) therefore conditions on everything that chose the units, and the selection is ignorable for that model: fp_occu() can use the clips without weighting them. This holds only when the size of every directed round came from a model of data that the new fit also holds. Design-based estimates from the clips alone, such as the precision of the classifier, still need the weights 1 / inclusion_prob that sheepdog records.

Experimental

This function is experimental (new after 2.3.0, part of the integration with 'sheepdog'): its arguments and results may change in a minor version, as sheepdog::select_directed() settles. See crywolf-api.

See also

fp_sites(), fp_read_sheepdog()

Examples

# \donttest{
# the small export of sheepdog shipped with crywolf
dir <- system.file("extdata", "sheepdog-export", package = "crywolf")
x <- suppressWarnings(fp_read_sheepdog(dir, species = "phy_cuv"))
auto <- fp_aggregate(x$occasions, x$detections, threshold = 0.5,
                     by = c("site", "occasion_id"), validation = x$validation)
m <- fp_occu(fp_data(auto, x$sites), random_recorder = FALSE,
             chains = 2, threads_per_chain = 1)
#> Warning: No verified data: the false-positive rate is identified only by the priors. Treat the estimates with caution.
#> Running MCMC with 2 parallel chains, with 1 thread(s) per chain...
#> 
#> Chain 1 finished in 0.6 seconds.
#> Chain 2 finished in 0.6 seconds.
#> 
#> Both chains finished successfully.
#> Mean chain execution time: 0.6 seconds.
#> Total execution time: 0.8 seconds.
#> 
units <- fp_review_priority(m, species_code = unique(x$detections$species_code),
                            validation = x$validation)
head(units)
#>   site                species_code       size
#> 1  BAI Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv 0.24625664
#> 2  ARA Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv 0.23085412
#> 3  XAR Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv 0.03659857
#> 4  NHE Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv 0.01294631
# then, in sheepdog, with the predictions of the survey:
# sel <- sheepdog::select_directed(pred, units, n_units = 10, threshold = 0.5)
# }
